title: Film, Review, Refine: A Practical Guide to Teacher Self-Coaching With Lesson Video
author: Tom Sherrington
source: Thinking Deeply about Primary Education, February 2, 2026
summary: Self-coaching through lesson video analysis transforms teaching practice by creating structured reflection opportunities. Teachers who film their lessons and review them systematically—focusing on specific aspects of practice rather than general impressions—build lasting instructional improvements. The process works because video provides objective evidence that counters intuition and bias, making it possible to see patterns in student engagement, pacing, and teacher moves that feel invisible in real time.
points: Video review must follow a narrow protocol: film, review, identify one specific change, implement it, then film again.
Teachers improve faster when they focus on one aspect at a time rather than trying to fix everything.
The feedback loop of observe-reflect-adjust creates deliberate practice conditions for teaching just as it does for athletic coaching.
quotes: The power of video is that it removes the guesswork and emotion from self-assessment.
Effective self-coaching requires a clear focus and a structured routine, not random viewing of your own lessons.
Small, intentional changes compound into significant shifts in teaching effectiveness over time.” Archived from Thinking Deeply about Primary Education on April 21, 2026 by Tim.
